### 2026-10-11 – October 11: Finished the firmware!

**3.82h**

October 11: Finished the firmware!

I finished the firmware part of the designing the pcb for week 1.

Time spent this session: 2 hours

Today I finished the firmware for my Desk Pet Starbie project. I spent around 2 hours working on it. . I didn't really know what I was doing at the start, (i mean i still don't understand all of it lol) so I had to spend a lot of time going through the code and figuring out what each part was for.

Thankfully some Ai help on explaining what the code did really helped me.

After a while I started on actually working on the project firmware. I downloaded all the drivers that were needed and selected the correct board in the Arduino IDE. Once I got the setup working, I decided to take a quick break to go eat and then return to start the work.
Luckily, most of the main work had already been done by the guide (tysm) , so I didn't have to make the entire firmware from scratch. I mostly had to understand the existing code and change a few things to make it fit my version of the Starbie project.

I added trail effect, as the guide told me to. The original project guide used a star trail, but I didn't really think that fit the theme I was going for. Since I wanted Starbie to have an aquatic theme, I changed the trail into bubbles instead. I also somehow managed to add a random size bubble effect and make it slightly more bubbly , which i hope it works. I also changed the sprite into a jellyfish, which made a lot more sense with the whole underwater theme. And the jellyfish looks so cute with the smile and all. I used Piskel to design the sprite and image2cpp to use it.

By the end of the session, I had the firmware working and the main features I wanted were finished. And now we hope it actually works ! :)
